SAN-09-001.verdict: IN SCOPE — Law-3 footgun, NOT a reckless admin mistake. KEPT.
SAN-09-001.surpriseTest: MET, and unusually strongly. The contract's own NatSpec at PhlimboV3.sol:445-447 actively tells a reader that blocklisted recipients are handled ('the flush must never brick'), and the story-027 suite models blocked recipients in six tests. A competent, non-malicious owner would reasonably conclude the blocklist case is covered protocol-wide. It is covered on the ROTATION path only; the everyday SELF-SERVICE path reverts and freezes staker principal. The documentation does not merely fail to warn — it affirmatively misleads. Surprise is guaranteed => footgun => in scope.
SAN-09-001.notAdminMistake: There is no owner misconfiguration here at all. The trigger is a third party (the token issuer) blocklisting a staker; the owner does nothing wrong and the staker does nothing wrong. Classifying this as an admin mistake would be a category error.

SAN-09-002.surpriseTest: MET. SolvencyDetermination.md:43-44 — REGENERATED IN THIS VERY RANGE — asserts emission 'is recomputed on every stake/withdraw; it cannot exceed what the APY implies'. The PoC exceeds it by 8.5x. The doc's own wording enumerates stake/withdraw and silently omits pauseWithdraw; the omission IS the gap. pauseWithdraw's own docblock (:581-594) enumerates the V3 deltas and the deliberate exiter forfeit but never states the emission rate is left stale.
SAN-09-002.notAdminMistake: No attacker and no owner error is required — the trigger is any staker exiting during any ROUTINE promo rotation. V3's beginFlush (:429-437) pauses on EVERY rotation, so the window is scheduled and mempool-visible, not an emergency. The harm lands on THIRD PARTIES (survivors receive unbacked phUSD; phUSD holders are diluted), so no 'penalty on the exiter' semantics apply.

SAN-09-004.surpriseTest: MET. PhlimboV3.sol:322-323 states UNCONDITIONALLY that a retired token's bank 'is unreachable here and stays pullable via claimUnclaimablePromo'. That is only true while the token is not re-promoted. A competent owner running a routine second campaign with the same partner token would not expect it to silently re-arm the sweep over an old bank.
SAN-09-004.ejectorSeatCompliance: VERIFIED COMPLIANT. This finding proposes NO accounting inside emergencyTransfer. The standing memo (ejector-seat principle; pe7m2 closed INVALID) is honoured — the OBVIOUS face (owner sweeps a live bank, documented) was already suppressed upstream by the deduplicator at DROP-09-06 and is NOT re-filed. What survives is filed against the DOC and against startPromotion, which are not the ejector seat.

foTPrecedentChecked.appliedThisRun: NO — and deliberately so. That precedent covers GENUINE fee-on-transfer-token findings: a non-standard token whose transfer moves less than `amount`. NOT ONE finding in this run's surviving set is of that kind. SAN-09-001 and SAN-09-009 concern a BLOCKLISTING token whose transfer REVERTS OUTRIGHT — a different mechanism, a different victim (the staker's principal, not the owner's retryable funding call), and a different consequence (unrecoverable-by-self-service freeze, not a revert-and-retry). Stretching the FoT precedent to cover a blocklist revert would be exactly the over-broad known-invalid match Law 1 forbids. USDT — explicitly carved OUT of the weird-ERC20 exclusion by C4 — is itself a blocklisting token, and the finding names USDC (the protocol's plausible stable) as the realistic vector.

The leak does not route through permissionless collectReward — stake calls _updatePool() at :648 BEFORE _updatePhUSDEmissionRate() at :674, so the FIRST post-unpause stake settles the whole elapsed window at the stale rate and only then repairs it. The PoC calls NO collectReward and still measures 8.5x. REMEDIATION CONSEQUENCE: gating collectReward would NOT fix this.

ARMING PROPERTY — worth reporting REGARDLESS of the current APY value: the finding is armed by any future setDesiredAPY commit, a two-tx owner action with no warning that it activates a mint leak. If the live config is zero-APY, the finding is DORMANT, not invalid.

Absolute magnitude anchored on ~68,212 phUSD live supply (carried from run-08) and 5% APY (docstring :63); the leak scales linearly in both. Flush window modelled at 1 day but owner-controlled and unbounded in principle. Because claim() never repairs the rate (:738-764), the leak runs until the first post-unpause stake/withdraw — read the per-day figure as a RATE, not a total.

findings.severityBasis: LOW, not Medium. The deciding question the manual-review record left open (does the migrator's withdraw leg bypass the blocked recipient?) IS NOW RESOLVED IN THE AFFIRMATIVE, source-verified by the sanitizer at MigratorV2V3.sol:250 — `phlimboV2.withdraw(amount, user)` is called BY THE MIGRATOR, so the migrator is msg.sender and therefore the beneficiary of the auto-claimed rewards; the blocked user is never the transfer recipient on that path. This is the same argument that closed V3-M-01. No asset loss, TWO owner-mediated rescues, and migration cures it outright.

LEDGER_CAVEAT_MUST_ATTACH.headline: THE MIGRATION RESCUE EVAPORATES ON MIGRATION COMPLETION — this caveat is the reason the finding cannot simply be closed once migration finishes.
LEDGER_CAVEAT_MUST_ATTACH.detail: The severity downgrade to Low rests on TWO rescues: (a) the migrator routing at MigratorV2V3.sol:250, and (b) a full-pauseWithdraw escape. Rescue (a) is TEMPORARY: when migration completes and the owner unwires the migrator via setMigrator(0), rescue (a) DISAPPEARS. The remaining path is setPauser -> pause -> full pauseWithdraw.
LEDGER_CAVEAT_MUST_ATTACH.sharpeningFactSourceVerified: PhlimboV2's pause() is PAUSER-ONLY — `require(msg.sender == pauser, "Only pauser can pause")` at src/PhlimboV2.sol:270. V3 by contrast grants the owner a direct pause — `require(msg.sender == pauser || msg.sender == owner(), ...)` at src/PhlimboV3.sol:576. So on V2 the surviving rescue additionally depends on the owner FIRST controlling or re-appointing the pauser (setPauser). Both lines read and confirmed by the sanitizer this run.
LEDGER_CAVEAT_MUST_ATTACH.triageConsequence: Do NOT close this finding on the reasoning 'migration will cure it'. Migration curing it and migration REMOVING THE RESCUE are the same event. If any V2 staker is blocklisted at the moment the migrator is unwired, the cheap rescue is gone and the remaining one is a three-step pauser-mediated escape on a contract whose pause() the owner does not directly control.

notFindings.item: PhlimboV3.sol:518 / finalizePromotion — Aderyn ADERYN-013 'state change after external call' (unguarded CEI).
notFindings.verdict: REFUTED. NOT a finding. NOT filed. NOT fingerprinted.
notFindings.reasoning: The reentrancy is harmless: a re-entrant finalizePromotion recomputes `leftover = balance > banked ? balance - banked : 0` against the ALREADY-REDUCED balance and gets 0, so there is no double sweep; the outer frame then zeroes state the inner frame already zeroed — idempotent. Re-entry additionally requires a callback-bearing promo token, excluded by the profiler's token trust assumption and owner-selected.

RECORDED_AS_QA_DEFENCE_IN_DEPTH_NOTE.why: THE PROTECTION IS INCIDENTAL, NOT DESIGNED. It rests on beginFlush's pause, the :281 unpause bar, the :513 cursor requirement and the :824 phase gate — four unrelated invariants, none of which exists to protect finalizePromotion. A future change could remove any of them without anyone noticing this function was relying on it. That is the shape of a latent Law-1 exploit even though it is not one today.
RECORDED_AS_QA_DEFENCE_IN_DEPTH_NOTE.recommendation: Add a one-line `nonReentrant` to finalizePromotion as cheap defence-in-depth. The function signature is `function finalizePromotion(address leftoverRecipient) external onlyOwner {` — it carries no guard, unlike batchClaim/stake/withdraw/claim/collectReward/claimUnclaimablePromo which all do.
